title: Judge a reading as defensible, not true
statement: Check an interpretation by whether the text contradicts it and whether a careful reader could defend it from the passage, keeping truth checks for plain claims.
detail: The lesson engine's video essay can pose two readings of a passage as an argument. Drafts were held when an argument beat's narration failed a check that everything it said was true, and when the judge could not defend a reading from the lines (`g9/transformer/v02/QA.md`, lines 177-178). Now an argument beat's narration has only to avoid saying anything the passage contradicts and each reading must be one a careful reader could defend from the passage as an answer to the lesson question, while other beats keep the check that everything they say is true to the passage (`g9/transformer/src/mechanics/video-essay.js`, lines 122-134); a reading's points now keep close to the lines' own words (`g9/transformer/v02/QA.md`, line 178). It bears on When reference facts don't cover a claim, which asks whether a judge should fail only a claim its facts contradict.
against: Narration that states what the text says is still held to being true: "Is everything narration_${k} says true to passage?" (g9/transformer/src/mechanics/video-essay.js line 126).
